mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that boosts equity markets, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during easing periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 6% triggers a negative signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as higher unemployment reduces consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) both increase, it signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window for this interaction-driven signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average triggers a negative signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as reduced production indicates slowing economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) interact to predict S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days; when FEDFUNDS is low and CPIAUCSL is high, it signals an inflationary environment that may lead to negative returns.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window for this interaction-driven signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during expansion periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) predicts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days; when UNRATE is low and PAYEMS is high, it signals a strong labor market that may lead to positive returns.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window for this interaction-driven signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 900 thousand units triggers a negative signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as reduced housing construction indicates slowing economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite negative signal.
